description: Connects your webinar to your own email list at Mailchimp, GetResponse or a similar provider, so every new registrant is posted there as well. Take it when sign-ups should land in your list from now on: "Put the registrations into my Mailchimp list." It needs the session, the webinar and the form address your provider gave you, plus the field names that provider expects for email, first name, last name and phone when it uses its own. Only what your provider's documentation says belongs here, nothing guessed. Existing registrants are not sent again. Test the connection afterwards with wi_test_webinar_autoresponder, and for the fields the participant fills in there is a separate tool. Side effect: it acts on your connected WordPress site; nothing else is touched. Words hosts use: connect Mailchimp, email list, autoresponder, GetResponse, sign-ups to my list

confirm.description: Only after the site answered code admin_editing: the host agreed to overwrite unsaved changes in wp-admin.

email_field.description: The provider's field name for the email address, e.g. EMAIL.

lastname_field.description: The provider's field name for the last name.

name_field.description: The provider's field name for the first name.

phone_field.description: The provider's field name for the phone number.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

url.description: The form action address the email provider gave the host.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

name: wi_change_webinar_autoresponder
title: Connect the webinar to an email list
